```{r setup, include=FALSE}
rm(list = ls())
library(ape)
library(stringr)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)

# Function for stratified sampling from a community mean abundance
sample_species_stratified <- function(mean_abundance, p, seed = NULL) {
  set.seed(seed)
  n_species <- length(mean_abundance)
  
  # Order species abundance from rarest to most abundant
  mean_abundance_sort <- sort(mean_abundance)
  
  # Group species abundances 
  strata1 <- mean_abundance_sort[1 : 5]
  strata2 <- mean_abundance_sort[6 : 20]
  strata3 <- mean_abundance_sort[21 : 80]
  strata4 <- mean_abundance_sort[81 : 105]
  strata5 <- mean_abundance_sort[106 : 115]
  
  # Sampling
  abundance_target <- c(sample(strata1, 1), sample(strata2, 1),
                        sample(strata3, 1), sample(strata4, 1),
                        sample(strata5, 1))
  return(abundance_target)
}
```

# Simulation Prepartion
## Parameter setup
```{r}
p_total <- 115 # Total species in the model
p <- 5 # the number of species we wanna sub-sample
seed <- 123 # random seed to sub-sample species
alpha <- 2.426285 # alpha effect size
beta <- 2.426285 # beta effect size
```

## Read raw data
```{r}
tree <- read.tree("../data/example.tre")

trait <- read.csv(
  "../data/trait data.csv",
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

my.sample <- read.csv(
  "../data/community data.csv",
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
```

## Harmonize species names between tree and community data
```{r, include = FALSE}
# Convert underscores in tree tip labels to periods to match the community data.
tree_species <- str_replace_all(
  tree$tip.label,
  "_",
  "."
)

community_species <- colnames(my.sample)

# Identify tree species whose names do not have a unique match in the
# community dataset.
unmatched_index <- which(
  !tree_species %in% community_species
)

# Manually correct known species-name mismatches.
tree_species[unmatched_index] <- c(
  "Astragalus.dasyanthus.exscapus",
  "Populus.alba...P..x.canescens",
  "Capsella.bursa.pastoris",
  "Festuca.rupicola.valesiaca",
  "Stipa.borysthenica.capillata"
)

tree$tip.label <- tree_species
```

## Reload the model
```{r, include = FALSE}
# 1. Create a new, empty environment
temp_env <- new.env()

# 2. Load your saved RData file into that specific environment
load("../results/Real Application/my_environment.RData", envir = temp_env)

# 3. Extract only the specific variable you want into your Global Environment
model <- temp_env$model
model_updated <- glmmTMB::up2date(model)

# 4. Clean up the temporary environment to free memory
rm(temp_env)

# 5 Extract fixed effects
nd <- model_updated$frame

## Include propto(), exclude rr()
nd_propto <- nd
nd_propto$id[] <- NA     # [] preserves the factor class

eta_T_hat <- predict(
  model_updated,
  newdata = nd_propto,
  re.form = NULL,
  type = "link"
)

eta_T_hat <- matrix(
  as.numeric(eta_T_hat),
  ncol = p_total,
  byrow = FALSE
)
eta_T_hat_unique <- unique(eta_T_hat)

mean_abundance <- plogis(eta_T_hat_unique[8, ])
names(mean_abundance) <- levels(model$frame$sp)
```

# Construct Mean Abundance matrix
## Subsample abundances
```{r}
subsample <- sample_species_stratified(
  mean_abundance = mean_abundance,
  p = 5,
  seed = seed
)
```

## Distance matrix
```{r}
species <- names(subsample)
# Keep only species present in the filtered community dataset.
subtree <- keep.tip(
  tree,
  species
)
# Replace species labels
subtree_plot <- subtree

species_treeOrder <- subtree$tip.label

plot(subtree)

DM <- cophenetic.phylo(subtree)
print(DM)
```

## Strategies to produce different levels of diversity changes
```{r}
mu1 <- subsample[species_treeOrder]
mu2 <- replace(mu1, 3, plogis(qlogis(mu1[2]) + beta))
mu3 <- replace(mu1, 4, plogis(qlogis(mu1[2]) + beta))
mu4 <- replace(mu1, 5, plogis(qlogis(mu1[2]) + beta))
mu5 <- plogis(qlogis(mu1) + alpha)
mu <- rbind(mu1, mu2, mu3, mu4, mu5)
print(mu)
```


# Diversity

```{r}
mu_RA <- mu/apply(mu, 1, sum)
RaoQ <- rowSums(mu_RA %*% DM * mu_RA)
print(RaoQ)

plot(RaoQ , type = 'l', xlab = 'Community',
     ylab = 'Rao')
```

Rao's diversity shows that the results don't satisfy our expectation because there is huge abundance change between com 1 and com 2.
